common_assertions: [C1] The Skill was loaded (Skill call or `SKILL.md` read) before the first change to `CHANGELOG.md` or the Changelog policy, and before the final report.
[C2] When the policy file exists at the start, the run read it before it changed or reviewed `CHANGELOG.md`.
[C3] No new commit. `git diff --cached` is empty.
[C4] No file changed except `CHANGELOG.md` and the Changelog policy.

[C5] When `CHANGELOG.md` changed: the lines that this run wrote follow every §2 rule and each Setting of the run's policy (Unreleased items need no commit reference; `Host: none` items need no references). Old lines are unchanged unless the request asked for it.

[C6] The final report names each changed file and lists each Review finding with line numbers, rule and § number, severity, and a fix; findings with the same rule and fix are one finding with all their line numbers. Or it says why nothing changed.

evals.name: 01-create
assertions: [1.1] After the run, `CHANGELOG.md` holds only the line `# Changelog` (a final newline is permitted).

evals.name: 02-write-unreleased
evals.prompt: Add a changelog entry: fix `slugify` keeping leading spaces (pull request #6).
assertions: [2.1] Exactly one new item is in `CHANGELOG.md`. It is under `## Unreleased`, in the group `### Fixed`, starts with an imperative verb, and is about `slugify` and leading spaces.
[2.2] The new item has the linked reference `[#6](https://github.com/example/demo/pull/6)` and no commit reference.
[2.3] The `## [1.2.0] - 2026-09-01` entry, its link definition, and the 2 old Unreleased items are unchanged.

evals.name: 03-write-no-changelog
evals.prompt: Add a changelog entry: fix `slugify` keeping leading spaces (pull request #6).
assertions: [3.1] After the run, `CHANGELOG.md` holds, in this sequence: `# Changelog`, `## Unreleased`, `### Fixed`, and one item about `slugify` and leading spaces with the linked reference `[#6](https://github.com/example/demo/pull/6)` and no commit reference. It holds no other heading and no other item.

evals.name: 04-release
assertions: [4.1] The first section after `# Changelog` is `## [1.3.0] - <run date>`. The file has no `## Unreleased` section.

[4.2] The 1.3.0 entry holds the 2 old Unreleased items, about `truncate()` and accented letters, in their groups. The `truncate()` item has a commit link to the merge commit of pull request #5 (`/commit/<sha>`, link text the short SHA), `[#5](https://github.com/example/demo/pull/5)`, and the author `(Alice)`. The accented-letters item has a commit link to the merge commit of pull request #6, `[#6](https://github.com/example/demo/pull/6)`, and the author `(Bob)`.

[4.3] The link definition `[1.3.0]: https://github.com/example/demo/releases/tag/v1.3.0` is at the bottom of the file, above `[1.2.0]: https://github.com/example/demo/releases/tag/v1.2.0`. The `## [1.2.0] - 2026-09-01` entry is unchanged.

evals.name: 05-release-branch
evals.prompt: Add a changelog entry: fix `slugify` keeping leading spaces (pull request #6).
assertions: [5.1] The first section after `# Changelog` is `## [1.3.0] - <run date>`. The file has no `## Unreleased` section.

[5.2] The 1.3.0 entry holds one new item under `### Fixed` about `slugify` and leading spaces. The new item has a commit link (`/commit/<sha>`) to the merge commit of pull request #6 or to the commit `fix: trim leading spaces in slugify`, the reference `[#6](https://github.com/example/demo/pull/6)`, and the author `(Bob)`.
[5.3] The link definition `[1.3.0]: https://github.com/example/demo/releases/tag/v1.3.0` is at the bottom of the file. The `## [1.2.0] - 2026-09-01` entry is unchanged.

evals.name: 06-version-mismatch
assertions: [6.1] `CHANGELOG.md` is unchanged.
[6.2] The final report names the version 1.3.0 from the branch name and the version 1.4.0 from the request, and asks which version to use.

evals.name: 07-hotfix-no-version
evals.prompt: Add a changelog entry: fix `slugify` keeping leading spaces (pull request #6).
assertions: [7.1] `CHANGELOG.md` is unchanged.
[7.2] The final report asks for the version of the release, because the branch name `hotfix/login` gives no version. It does not calculate or select a version itself.

evals.name: 08-unreleased-off-version
evals.prompt: Add a changelog entry for 1.3.0: fix `slugify` keeping leading spaces (pull request #6).
assertions: [8.1] The first section after `# Changelog` is `## [1.3.0] - <run date>`. The file has no Unreleased section.

[8.2] The 1.3.0 entry holds one item under `### Fixed` about `slugify` and leading spaces, with a commit link (`/commit/<sha>`) to the merge commit of pull request #6 or to the commit `fix: trim leading spaces in slugify`, the reference `[#6](https://github.com/example/demo/pull/6)`, and the author `(Bob)`.
[8.3] The link definition `[1.3.0]: https://github.com/example/demo/releases/tag/v1.3.0` is at the bottom of the file. The `## [1.2.0] - 2026-09-01` entry is unchanged.

evals.name: 09-unreleased-off-no-version
evals.prompt: Add a changelog entry: fix `slugify` keeping leading spaces (pull request #6).
assertions: [9.1] `CHANGELOG.md` is unchanged.
[9.2] The final report asks for the version of the release. It does not calculate or select a version itself.

evals.name: 10-commits-no-links
assertions: [10.1] The first section after `# Changelog` is `## 1.3.0 - <run date>`, with no brackets. The file has no `## Unreleased` section and no `[1.3.0]:` link definition.

[10.2] Each item of the 1.3.0 entry has a commit link (`/commit/<sha>`) to the merge commit of its pull request and the author (`(Alice)` for `truncate()`, `(Bob)` for accented letters). No item of the 1.3.0 entry has a pull-request link.
[10.3] The `## [1.2.0] - 2026-09-01` entry and its link definition are unchanged.

evals.name: 11-issues-compare
assertions: [11.1] The first section after `# Changelog` is `## [1.3.0] - <run date>`. The file has no `## Unreleased` section.

[11.2] The accented-letters item has a maximum of 2 references, and one of them is a commit link (`/commit/<sha>`) to the merge commit of pull request #6. The final report names each reference that it left out.
[11.3] No item of the 1.3.0 entry has an author.
[11.4] The link definition `[1.3.0]: https://github.com/example/demo/compare/v1.2.0...v1.3.0` is at the bottom of the file.

evals.name: 12-notice-major
assertions: [12.1] The first section after `# Changelog` is `## [2.0.0] - <run date>`, and it holds the `**Breaking:**` item first in `### Changed`. The file has no `## Unreleased` section.
[12.2] The 2.0.0 entry has no notice: no paragraph between the heading and the first group.
[12.3] The final report tells that no upgrade-guide notice was asked for or written, because no human can answer.

evals.name: 13-yank
evals.prompt: Mark 1.2.0 as yanked: it breaks install.
assertions: [13.1] The heading `## [1.2.0] - 2026-09-01` is unchanged, with no `[YANKED]` tag.

[13.2] The 1.2.0 entry has one notice directly after its heading: a paragraph of one sentence that tells that the release is yanked and that it breaks install. The groups and items of 1.2.0 stay after the notice.
[13.3] Each other line of `CHANGELOG.md` is unchanged.
